- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mean to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 price points in history show strong downward momentum, model should not overshoot downward — cap forecast decline at 1–2% below recent low.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.9 to -0.3) within 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect mean reversion toward 1–2 prior-day levels, not extreme extremes.  
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 10-day average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — model should not sell off prematurely.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day to correct for overconfidence bias.  
- For sentiment history with high volatility (±0.5+ swings), apply smoothing: forecast = weighted average of last 5–7 days + sentiment-adjusted drift (e.g., +0.1 if sentiment >0.7, -0.1 if <0.3).
